summary:
The ink module was already solid; I found and fixed 10 real problems, added 31 unit tests and 3 e2e tests, and everything passes. Status for the user ("Situación?"): nothing in this module is blocked. It is not ready to sell until src/data saves samples and settings (it is still a stub) and someone tries it on a real iPad with Apple Pencil and an Android tablet with S Pen.

What I checked: every file in src/ink (except ml/) against src/types/ink.ts and the specification; typecheck and tests; and fresh screenshots of every gallery entry on iPad, Android and iPad portrait, which I looked at. Spanish copy is correct and warm. The school stroke-order models are right. Contracts match.

Fixes:
1. CalibrationFlow saved samples under the active child, not its `childId` prop. During onboarding the new child may not be active yet, so samples were lost (in memory only, never stored). They now go to `childId`; they personalise the recogniser only when that child is the active one, or when there is none.
2. CalibrationFlow dropped samples silently if the model was still loading. It now waits up to about 6 s.
3. CalibrationFlow learned scribbles as digits. When the recogniser says "not a digit", the child is asked once "¡Uy! No lo he visto bien. ¿Otra vez?"; the second try is accepted.
4. Palm guard was missing on CalibrationFlow's Borrar and Saltar, which sit below-right of the pad where a right-handed palm rests. It was also missing on all five TraceDigit buttons, which sit to the right of the tracing area.
5. Personal samples were passed to the recogniser in an order that clashed with its "last = newest, keep 30 per digit" rule, so frequent corrections could push out calibration samples, and memory grew without limit. Now each digit keeps the newest 4 calibration, 10 corrected and 16 confirmed samples, oldest first, with duplicates dropped and memory bounded. The database keeps everything.
6. A cell that unmounted left its pending recognition behind, so a later confirm() could store a wrong answer's digit as a confirmed sample. Cells now forget it 2.5 s after unmounting (confirm() right after the answer still counts). It is guarded against React StrictMode's fake remount, which would otherwise erase fresh recognitions in dev.
7. InkProvider: after setPreferred(), a later change of the stored setting (for example by an adult) was ignored for the rest of the session. The stored setting now wins again once it changes.
8. Faded "ghost" pen strokes looked beaded (semi-transparent overlapping segments). They are now drawn as one path.
9. NumberInput with the keypad open: "6 × 7 =" lined up with the keypad, not the pad. Added `keypadPosition: 'below' | 'right'`; 'right' puts a 3×4 keypad beside the pad.
10. Lost Pencil dead end: once a pen has been seen, fingers can't write, and nothing told the child. Now, if the pen hasn't touched the screen for 3 s:
   - a finger on a lone DigitCell opens the digit picker;
   - inside a CellGroup or NumberInput, the keypad toggle wiggles with a bubble "¿Sin lápiz? ¡Toca aquí!";
   - CalibrationFlow says "¡Escribe con el lápiz!" and TraceDigit says "¡Repasa con el lápiz!".
   The capture engine reports this through a new onBlockedWrite callback.

Also fixed:
- A palm resting on a neighbouring cell no longer takes focus (that moved the keypad target and showed the × button under the palm); a finger now takes focus only when it really taps.
- A finger tap whose pointerup was lost no longer fires a phantom tap.
- Live real-model entries moved to `src/ink/live.gallery.tsx`. The scripted demos replay synthetic strokes that steal focus, which made the keyboard e2e fail during this review.
- Calibration pad is bigger on portrait tablets; the TraceDigit tip line keeps its height.
- InkProvider got a `penSeen` override (not saved) so tests and the gallery can show palm-rejection states.

Visual verdict: friendly and polished. The place-value colours, typeset digits over faded ink, keypad, alternative chips, stroke-order models with numbered green start dots, trace stars and calibration screen hold up on iPad and Android.
tests:
- `npm run typecheck 2>&1 | grep src/ink | grep -v src/ink/ml` → 0 lines. The only typecheck errors in the repo are 2 in src/audio/music.test.ts, which is another agent's work.
- `npx vitest run src/ink --exclude 'src/ink/ml/**'` → 14 files, 115 tests, all pass (was 11 files, 84 tests).
  - New test files: InkProvider.test.tsx (4), CalibrationFlow.test.tsx (7), TraceDigit.test.tsx (3).
  - Tests added to existing files:
    - learning: ordering and caps, duplicates, bounded memory, calibration for another child.
    - capture: blocked finger write, palm doesn't take focus, no phantom tap.
    - policy: msSincePenContact.
    - render: ghost strokes drawn as one path.
    - DigitCell: lost-Pencil picker, nothing while the pen is busy (palm), group nudge, unmount forgetting, StrictMode safety.
    - NumberInput: nudge and keypadPosition="right".
  - The tests for the preference override, the model-loading wait and the StrictMode remount fail on the old code.
- `npx playwright test tests/e2e/ink.spec.ts` → 6 passed, twice in a row, with the real model:
  - keyboard fill and clear;
  - pen-drawn 7, 1, 4, 0;
  - all ten digits drawn in the app's own Spanish school stroke order — none misread;
  - a scribble-out erases a cell;
  - 42, 56, 48, 63 and 72 written in the NumberInput with school digits;
  - "47" segmented and sent with ✓.
- `npx oxlint src/ink` (excluding ml) → 0 errors; only warnings for deliberate mount-only effects and a refs-in-closure heuristic that was already there.
openIssues: src/data is still a stub, so addInkSample, listInkSamples and updateChild do nothing: handwriting samples and the input preference are not saved until the data agent lands.

No real-device check yet. Synthetic pointer events are untrusted, so penSeen, iPadOS system palm rejection and the S Pen barrel-button eraser still need a test on an iPad with Apple Pencil and an Android tablet with S Pen.

Controlled-component limit: if a cell's value stays null from one exercise to the next (unreadable ink, or nothing submitted), there is no signal to clear the ink. Activities should mount a fresh DigitCell, NumberInput or CellGroup per exercise (key={exercise.id}).
TraceDigit can only be completed by tracing (no keyboard path). Whoever shows it should offer a skip.
The --cell-size-sm token (carry cells) is about 49px on iPad landscape, below the 56px tap minimum, which is tight for finger writing; bigCells (×1.2) helps. The token belongs to the integrator.
The database keeps every ink sample forever (the app only uses the newest 30 per digit). The data module may want to prune old 'confirmed' samples.
There is still no playwright.config.ts; the spec uses absolute URLs and Playwright's defaults.
CompanionArt is still the integrator's emoji stub in CalibrationFlow.
contractRequests: src/types/ink.ts DigitCellProps.onChange info: add `recognitionFix?: boolean`. DigitCell already sends it at runtime, typed as InkChangeInfo.
Document the extra hooks in the contract: useInkLearning().recognitionFixes() fills AttemptInput.recognitionFixes; read it before confirm() or discard(), which reset it.

Optional, adult settings: expose useInputMode().forgetPen() (e.g. 'Ya no uso lápiz en este dispositivo'). The in-game finger fallback now shows the keypad, but fingers only write again after forgetPen().
Optional: InkSample.modelId. image28 is always stored, so embeddings can be recomputed after a model update.
notesForOtherModules: Activities: mount a fresh DigitCell, NumberInput or CellGroup per exercise (key={exercise.id}). Setting value to null only clears the ink when the previous value was not null.

Activities: after a correct answer, call useInkLearning().confirm() in the submit handler. Within 2.5 s of the cells unmounting is fine; later than that, the pending digits are forgotten on purpose. After a wrong answer call discard(). Read recognitionFixes() first.

Activities: when NumberInput sits inline after an equation ('6 × 7 = [pad]'), pass keypadPosition="right" so the question stays level with the pad when the keypad is shown. With the question above the pad, the default 'below' is fine.
world-core onboarding: CalibrationFlow now stores samples for its childId prop even if that child is not active yet; no need to set the active child first.
Gallery: scripted demos are at /dev/gallery?only=src/ink/ink.gallery. The real-model entries used by tests/e2e/ink.spec.ts are at /dev/gallery?only=src/ink/live.gallery.

Once a pen has been seen on a device, fingers never write on ink surfaces (palm rejection). If the pen has been idle for 3 s, a finger opens the digit picker on a lone DigitCell, or makes the CellGroup / NumberInput keypad toggle wiggle with '¿Sin lápiz? ¡Toca aquí!'. Keep keypadToggle on unless you give the child another fallback.
metrics: Real-model e2e: 10/10 digits drawn in Spanish school stroke order were read correctly; the answers 42, 56, 48, 63, 72 and 47 were read correctly in the NumberInput. Unit tests: 115 (was 84). Each digit keeps at most 30 personal samples (4 calibration, 10 corrected, 16 confirmed), matching the recogniser's per-digit limit; memory stays bounded however many samples the database returns.
